correctness.rationale: Natural-spline curvature equations form a nonsingular 2x2 system with determinant (r+2)(3r+2). Exact derivative cardinal coefficients on the three intervals reproduce affine data (coefficients sum 1). Minimizing over [1,K]^3 gives 1-(K-1)N pointwise. On the outer interval the sharp negative coefficient mass is 1/(r+2) at the left boundary; on the central interval positive b coefficient and the quadratic individual/matched negative terms yield N <= max{1/(r+2),r/[2(r+2)]}, with the second attained at its midpoint. The individual-negative bound is verified separately for r<=2 and r>=2; the analytic inequalities cover all real r>0. Exact extremal positive-secant triples (1,K,1) and (K,1,K) give actual negative derivatives above the threshold, and the branches meet uniquely at r=2. A separate standard-library exact-rational checker passed 5050 derivative evaluations, central-coefficient identities, and explicit strict witnesses. Finite tests only supplement the complete proof; no numerical root assumption.

originality.rationale: The claim optimizes the all-data sufficient-and-sharp secant-slope contrast for monotonicity of the unmodified natural cubic on symmetric four-knot meshes. Full published mathematical records on the same four-knot natural spline instead optimize unrestricted variation amplification, with different optimal gap ratios; the clamped four-knot threshold changes the boundary conditions. First-hand inspected external spline literature discusses pointwise Hermite criteria or end-slope adjustment, not the full uniform-in-data sharp mesh contrast threshold. No equivalent theorem or stronger covering result was found after aliases, mesh/slope terminology and implication comparisons. Literature priority remains provisional because no search proves absence of an earlier equivalence.
residual_risks: An older unindexed spline-shape-conditions result might state an equivalent uniform contrast cutoff or a more general theorem implying it.

The Fritsch–Carlson local conditions are classical; translating them into the unique global symmetric mesh optimum may be regarded as a corollary by specialists, although the exact minimax expression was not identified.
Not every historical spline monograph, thesis, or publisher-only paper is accessible; literature priority should be independently checked.

value.rationale: Even increasing data can be overshot by classical smooth interpolation; a sharp positivity-cone radius gives an actionable exact mesh design guarantee absent from generic sufficient shape-preservation inequalities. The theorem identifies two competing geometrically distinct failure mechanisms and proves their unique robust equalization on mesh (1,2,1), increasing admissible slope contrast from 4 to 5 (25%) relative to uniform spacing. The condition is natural (ratio of positive secant slopes), mesh and boundary hypotheses explicit, and both sharp obstructions are constructive. It concerns the first natural cubic with coupled interior curvatures, a useful benchmark for stable interpolation and monotone-data design; no general arbitrary-grid claim is implied.
